tasks.short: Summarize continuity exercises, assess recovery gaps, and recommend corrective actions.

steps.what: Collect the exercise objectives, scenario, schedule, and approved recovery procedures.
Export recorded exercise events, recovery timings, and unresolved incidents.
Debrief participants about decisions, workarounds, failures, and missing observations.
Reconcile event timings and calculate recovery performance against agreed targets.
Assess failure causes, evidence limits, business consequences, and corrective priorities.
Write the exercise report, covering preparation, execution, findings, conclusions, and recommendations.

loop.input: Report template, exercise references, calculated results, and the planner's assessed findings.
loop.output: Draft exercise report with source references and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections, source identifiers, and numerical consistency; planner reviews narrative accuracy.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; unresolved claims return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle tables and headings; varied observations require concise narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Approve the report and agree corrective owners, priorities, and deadlines.
Publish the approved report with its supporting evidence and access restrictions.
Record the approved corrective actions in the delivery tracker.

tasks.design: Configured exports from {HELPDESK} and references from {DOCS} feed deterministic recovery calculations on {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded drafting loop fills the report template using the planner's findings and traceable evidence. After the risk owner approves publication and corrective actions, {WORKFLOW} publishes to {DOCS} and creates actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence had inconsistent timestamps and separate document versions. Narrative assembly still required substantial manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, reusable templates, and faster code development make evidence assembly affordable. Bounded drafting can summarize supplied observations.
tasks.still_hard: Exercise logs rarely explain why people improvised. Conflicting accounts and unrealistic test conditions still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when an apparently successful recovery concealed unsafe workarounds or depended on one unusually capable person.

ambition.what: Cross-exercise recurring failure review

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling reports and more time comparing recurring weaknesses. The risk owner can delegate corrective-action prioritization within an agreed remediation budget.

reach.task: Turn approved recovery fixes into deliverable remediation work.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, acceptance criteria, and verification of action closure.

evidence.claim: Structured timestamps and recovery targets support deterministic calculations; causal conclusions need human assessment.
Source-constrained drafting is feasible, but the digest provides no continuity-report implementation case.
A documented report with nonexistent sources led to a partial refund, supporting explicit source validation.

assumptions: This describes a mid-size European company using document plans and a ticket-based exercise log.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The first build covers one exercise format and excludes automatic causal conclusions.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Whether exercise events are recorded in {HELPDESK}, documents, or another available slot.
Whether timestamps, recovery targets, and source versions are reliable.
Who can approve corrective spending and report distribution.
Whether observations contain personal data requiring additional access restrictions.
research_questions: Can the calculation reproduce the last exercise report and expose its missing evidence?
Does factual review take less time than drafting from scratch?
new_work: Review narrative claims and unresolved timing exceptions.
Maintain report templates, target definitions, and source mappings.
Check that approved actions retain their owners and evidence links.
tasks.statement: Write reports to summarize testing activities, including descriptions of goals, planning, scheduling, execution, results, analysis, conclusions, and recommendations.

tasks.short: Keep application and network blueprints accurate for continuity planning and recovery.

steps.what: Export application-inventory and network-management records from the {OTHER}.
Ask service owners to explain missing components and recent technical changes.
Validate recovery dependencies, connection directions, and undocumented exceptions.
Redraw application and network blueprints using validated dependencies.
Check blueprint changes and approve the operational reference version.
Publish the approved blueprint and archive the superseded version.

tasks.design: An integration loads authorised application-inventory and network-management exports from the {OTHER} into dependency records on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks identify missing owners and changed relationships, generate diagrams, and route approval through the {WORKFLOW} before versioned publication in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical inventories and hand-drawn diagrams use different identifiers. Important recovery dependencies often exist only in service owners' knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable identifiers, available exports, and deterministic diagram generation can remove repeated transcription. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of adapters and diagram templates.
tasks.still_hard: An inventory cannot prove recovery behaviour. Hidden dependencies, restricted network information, and obsolete records still need technical validation.
tasks.human_edge: Service owners distinguish a visible connection from a dependency that determines recovery order.

ambition.what: A dependency-change brief for recovery exercise designers.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time drawing and more time resolving uncertain recovery dependencies. With an agreed mandate, they can return incomplete dependency submissions for correction; technical architecture decisions remain with IT owners.

reach.task: Maintain service dependency records used to assess technical changes.
reach.learn: Identifier conventions, dependency semantics, network zones, and evidence of recovery order.

evidence.claim: Blueprint maintenance can combine technical inventory exports, owner validation, diagram editing, and controlled publication.
Validated structured dependency records support deterministic diagram generation and change checks without a model loop.

assumptions: IT owners retain responsibility for technical accuracy; the planner coordinates the continuity view.
Application and network inventories provide exportable identifiers.
The first release uses authorised exports rather than active network discovery.
Build ranges cover a limited inventory scope and include access review and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether current inventories share reliable component identifiers.
Which dependencies are documented and which need interviews or recovery tests.
Whether existing software already generates adequate diagrams.
Restrictions on storing technical topology and required access approvals.
research_questions: Can existing configuration replace the proposed diagram generator?
Which relationship types are necessary to show recovery order?
How should a diagram display unknown or unverified dependencies?
new_work: Resolve unmatched identifiers and changed inventory schemas.
Validate flagged dependency changes with service owners.
Maintain diagram templates, access permissions, and publication checks.
tasks.statement: Maintain and update organization information technology applications and network systems blueprints.

tasks.short: Interpret applicable regulations and translate them into continuity obligations and controls.

steps.what: Retrieve relevant regulatory publications and check for changes.
Read changed clauses and prepare a referenced obligation summary.

loop.input: Versioned official texts, previous versions and recorded organisational scope.
loop.output: Candidate obligations with exact citations, dates, scope conditions and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Verify quotations and references against stored text; distinguish binding text from guidance and proposals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per changed text; missing or conflicting sources go to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Change detection is deterministic, but legal duties and exceptions are expressed across prose and cross-references.

steps.what: Determine applicability and approve interpretations with the continuity planner.
Compare approved obligations with current plans, controls and supporting evidence.

loop.input: Approved obligations, versioned controls, continuity plans and evidence references.
loop.output: Proposed obligation-to-control mappings and potential evidence gaps.
loop.check: Require source references for mappings; distinguish missing evidence from demonstrated noncompliance.
loop.stop: One mapping and one correction pass per obligation batch; ambiguous matches require planner review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Identifiers handle established mappings, but new obligations and controls often use different language.

steps.what: Agree corrective actions, owners and deadlines for confirmed gaps.
Update the obligation register and assign approved corrective actions.
Notify affected owners of approved obligations, actions and review dates.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks approved sources in the {GOV_PORTAL} and stores versioned texts in the {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and control-mapping loops produce referenced drafts for legal and operational review. Approved interpretations populate a register in the {WORKFLOW}, which assigns actions in the {PROJECT} and sends notices through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reliable applicability depended on organisational context, cross-references and professional interpretation. Source monitoring alone could not establish what the organisation needed to change.
tasks.enabler_now: Version comparison, source capture and approval registers are established techniques that are cheaper to assemble with AI-assisted coding. Bounded extraction reduces reading effort when citations are checked against the actual text.
tasks.still_hard: Sector, entity, jurisdiction and implementation details change applicability. Guidance can be ambiguous, and source coverage must be maintained.
tasks.human_edge: The planner connects legal interpretation to practical recovery controls and knows when an apparent compliance gap needs specialist advice.

ambition.what: Continuity obligation briefings for site supervisors

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching and copying clauses to testing applicability and resolving control gaps. The planner gains capacity to advise operational owners; legal interpretation and risk acceptance remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Map obligations to controlled procedures and evidence.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, corrective-action closure and procedure change control.

reach.task: Translate site obligations into emergency and recovery procedures.
reach.learn: Site-specific requirements, inspection evidence and operational constraints.

evidence.claim: Source monitoring, version comparison and obligation registers can use deterministic technology.
Applicability assessment needs organisational context and legal judgement beyond text extraction.
A government report containing nonexistent sources led to a partial refund.

assumptions: The pilot covers an approved, limited set of official sources and one organisational scope.
Legal counsel is available for material or ambiguous interpretations.
The register records evidence gaps separately from confirmed noncompliance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; national rules determine employment and consultation requirements.
Consent and access include legal-document permissions, source access and any required employee consultation.
Build estimates do not include a comprehensive regulatory content subscription or coverage of every jurisdiction.
unknowns: Which entities, countries, sectors and contractual obligations are in scope?
Which official sources and existing interpretations are authoritative?
Who may approve routine interpretations and which issues require external advice?
What employee consultation requirements apply under national rules or existing agreements?
research_questions: Which approved sources provide reliable change feeds or stable version identifiers?
Can reviewers consistently distinguish a missing document from an actual control failure?
What level of source context is needed to avoid losing exceptions and cross-references?
new_work: Maintain source coverage, organisational scope and interpretation review dates.
Check extracted citations, exceptions and effective dates.
Resolve ambiguous mappings and conflicting legal interpretations.
Repair changed source connections and monitor missed publications.
tasks.statement: Interpret government regulations and applicable codes to ensure compliance.

tasks.short: Select people or transactions for focused continuity intelligence collection.

steps.what: Review the intelligence question, collection remit and permitted sources.
Find dependency records, relevant transactions and business contacts across permitted sources.
Compare evidence and prepare a target shortlist with reasons and information gaps.

loop.input: Permitted source bundle and scope notes.
loop.output: Draft target shortlist with source-linked facts, reasons and information gaps.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and source references; a planner checks relevance, omissions and unsupported inferences.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction pass per bundle; unresolved evidence returns to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Incident narratives describe dependencies and relevant contacts in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Discuss operational context and choose proposed targets and collection priorities.
Approve targets, collection methods, limits and escalation conditions.
Record the approved scope and send the collection brief to assigned staff.

tasks.design: A read-only integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles permitted records from the {DOCS}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; a bounded model loop extracts source-linked facts for a draft shortlist. People choose targets and approve collection limits in the {WORKFLOW}, which generates the collection brief in the {DOCS} and routes it through the {EMAIL}. Collection itself remains a separate, explicitly scoped activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records sit across systems, names do not always match, and selecting a target depends on context. Bespoke retrieval and document preparation previously cost more than occasional use justified.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation and brief templates. Bounded text extraction helps prepare evidence, without resolving the underlying judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete dependencies, ambiguous identities and restricted sources remain difficult. GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use, while national rules may constrain employee-related collection.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently relevant person or transaction would distract from the continuity question, and judge whether further enquiry is proportionate.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of enquiries into newly exposed supplier dependencies.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing assumptions with process owners. Approval rights remain with the risk owner; no additional investigation authority is gained.

reach.task: Identify shipments whose disruption would interrupt a critical business process.
reach.learn: Shipment identifiers, route dependencies and the difference between delay signals and confirmed disruption.

reach.task: Trace a critical process to its supporting applications and interfaces.
reach.learn: Service dependency mapping, identifier matching and evidence freshness.

evidence.claim: Permission-aware retrieval, structured records and template generation can support evidence preparation.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare source-linked facts, while target selection still requires contextual human judgement.
The digest provides no direct continuity intelligence targeting case; build estimates and time reductions are design hypotheses.

assumptions: This unusual supplemental task concerns lawful continuity enquiries into relevant business contacts and transactions.
The company has a continuity planner or a risk specialist performing this work alongside other duties.
The risk owner approves sensitive collection scopes; routine authority may be delegated.
The initial build covers a limited set of accessible internal sources.
The access estimate includes employee or works-council consultation where national rules require it; formal proceedings may take longer.
Time shares favour judgement but allow substantial evidence preparation; they are estimates, not observations.
unknowns: Whether the actual remit is continuity, security, fraud or another intelligence function.
Which sources, collection methods and personal data categories are permitted.
Which role has authority to approve targets and collection limits.
Whether stable identifiers connect contacts, dependencies and transactions.
Which national rules and consultation arrangements apply.
Whether the existing {WORKFLOW} supports approvals and permission-controlled routing.
research_questions: Which recent enquiries changed a continuity decision, and what evidence made them useful?
How often does source retrieval miss relevant records or confuse identities?
Can existing {DOCS} search and templates handle enough preparation to avoid a model loop?
What review effort and omission rate does a representative pilot show?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and investigate missing or conflicting references.
Maintain source permissions, identifier mappings and connector checks.
Update brief templates and extraction instructions when collection remits change.
Apply retention limits to source bundles and decision records.
Check that routing remains within the approved collection scope.
tasks.statement: Identify individual or transaction targets to direct intelligence collection.

tasks.short: Maintain and test emergency call trees, contact details and escalation routes.

steps.what: Export permitted employee contacts and reporting lines from {HCM}.
Ask contact owners to confirm numbers and availability through {EMAIL}.
Agree primary callers, deputies, coverage periods and escalation rules.
Update call-tree branches and telephone lists in {SPREADSHEET}.
Approve call-tree changes, drill recipients, timing, channels and test wording.
Start the drill by calling initial recipients and recording contact attempts.
Answer drill calls, acknowledge receipt and telephone assigned downstream contacts.
Reconcile acknowledgements, failed contacts and elapsed times in {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Permitted contacts from {HCM} feed a restricted register in {WORKFLOW}, where contact owners confirm details and deterministic rules generate call trees and flag coverage gaps. After a controller approves the exact drill specification, configured {TELEPHONY} notifications collect acknowledgements, apply approved escalation rules and feed a readiness report in {BI}; a controlled offline tree supports manual fallback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact changes and deputy assignments were copied between personnel records and local lists. Automated calling needed reliable acknowledgements, approved escalation rules and access to permitted numbers.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, notification services and scheduling rules can handle most steps. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of contact synchronisation and deterministic coverage checks; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: A delivered message does not prove understanding or availability. Shared telecommunications outages and out-of-hours coverage remain operational constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Managers agree workable coverage, respect personal circumstances and distinguish a missed acknowledgement from a real welfare concern.

ambition.what: Monthly decision on unresolved emergency communication coverage gaps

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time copying phone lists and chasing routine confirmations, and more time resolving uncovered roles and fallback weaknesses. They can gain delegated authority to run drills within an approved schedule; real incident activation remains with the designated incident lead.

reach.task: Maintain out-of-hours departmental coverage and deputy arrangements.
reach.learn: Coverage planning, escalation design and contact-data stewardship.

evidence.claim: Contact synchronisation, graph checks, scheduled notifications and acknowledgement reporting can use deterministic technology.
The supplied human-task prior overstates manual necessity for list maintenance and drill administration; acknowledgement and coverage judgements still require people.
The digest supplies no directly evidenced emergency call-tree product or implementation case.

assumptions: Existing communication facilities support approved test messages and delivery or acknowledgement records.
Only authorised contact fields are synchronised; contact owners verify personal numbers.
Automated drill dispatch uses the controller-approved recipients, timing, wording and escalation limits.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; personal contact use, out-of-hours arrangements and employee monitoring require assessment under national rules.
Consultation estimates allow for applicable employee representation; elapsed negotiation time may exceed working-day effort.
unknowns: Permitted use and retention of personal telephone numbers.
Existing acknowledgement, retry and escalation capabilities.
Applicable employee consultation and out-of-hours arrangements.
Fallback channels during a shared communications outage.
research_questions: Does the drill need to test human relay behaviour as well as direct reachability?
Which fallback channels remain usable during the disruption scenarios being planned for?
new_work: Resolve unconfirmed contacts and uncovered deputy roles.
Maintain escalation limits, test wording and approved drill schedules.
Review failures without turning drill participation into employee performance scoring.
Test fallback routes and refresh offline call trees.
Maintain contact retention rules and notification usage costs.
tasks.statement: Establish, maintain, or test call trees to ensure appropriate communication during disaster.

tasks.short: Design and implement practical tools and services that reduce disruption risk.

steps.what: Collect recovery gaps, current procedures, and requests for improved continuity tools.
Agree operational needs, fallback arrangements, users, and acceptable recovery outcomes.
Compare approved solution patterns, costs, dependencies, and expected recovery coverage.
Select a solution and approve its scope, costs, limitations, and acceptance criteria.
Configure a prototype with forms, fallback checklists, escalation rules, and status records.
Test normal operation, lost connectivity, failed dependencies, and recovery acceptance criteria.
Authorize deployment after reviewing test evidence, residual risk, and rollback arrangements.
Deploy the approved configuration and verify access, ownership, and fallback availability.

tasks.design: A solution catalogue in {DOCS} and deterministic comparison on {DATA_PLATFORM} turn agreed requirements into transparent options. Approved templates in {WORKFLOW} provide continuity forms, checklists, escalation flows, and status records. Repeatable tests produce acceptance evidence before a risk owner authorizes deployment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each tool request became a small bespoke project. Requirements, dependencies, and acceptance tests were rarely reusable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow components and faster implementation of comparison and test utilities lower the cost of small tools. No model loop is needed for the scoped solution.
tasks.still_hard: A tool may fail during the same disruption it is meant to manage. Independent access, realistic recovery tests, and unsupported requirements remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Choose workable compromises between recovery speed, safety, cost, and the burden placed on operational teams.

ambition.what: Continuity tool clinic for small operational teams

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time shaping requirements and testing whether tools work under disruption. Delegated authority can let them approve small configurations within a defined budget and risk envelope.

reach.task: Specify and test continuity workflows and their failure modes.
reach.learn: Access design, dependency isolation, acceptance testing, and rollback planning.

reach.task: Validate fallback access when a workplace or building service is unavailable.
reach.learn: Physical access dependencies and practical workplace recovery constraints.

evidence.claim: Forms, records, rule-based escalation, and comparisons can be built from configured components and deterministic code.
Recovery tools require testing against shared dependencies and loss of their usual access path.
The digest contains no direct implementation case for continuity-tool design or its expected savings.

assumptions: The typical case is a small internal workflow or records tool, not replacement of critical infrastructure.
An existing {WORKFLOW} supports the necessary configuration and access controls.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are estimates for one limited tool.
Human tests remain necessary for physical and organisational failure scenarios.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Which existing configuration capabilities and reusable components are available.
Whether recovery access depends on the same infrastructure as normal operations.
Which integrations can operate during an outage.
Who can accept residual risk and authorize deployment.
Whether the tool processes employee data or changes working arrangements.
research_questions: Which requests can be satisfied by existing configuration without a new application?
Can users complete the recovery workflow when normal identity, network, or workplace access fails?
new_work: Maintain approved solution patterns and realistic cost assumptions.
Test configuration changes and shared dependency failures.
Handle requirements that exceed existing component capabilities.
Keep deployment, rollback, and fallback instructions current.
tasks.statement: Design or implement products and services to mitigate risk or facilitate use of technology-based tools and methods.

tasks.short: Build and obtain approval for continuity and disaster recovery budgets.

steps.what: Retrieve actual expenditure, commitments and current budget limits.
Collate quotations and staffing estimates supplied by procurement and service owners.

loop.input: Received quotations and staffing estimates with their dates and source files.
loop.output: Cost assumptions with units, currency, exclusions, validity dates and source references.
loop.check: Validate totals and units; flag missing tax treatment, recurring charges and ambiguous exclusions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per file; ambiguous entries go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured submissions need only validation, but received quotations also contain material conditions in prose.

steps.what: Calculate recovery-option costs, cash timing and contingency allowances.
Compare affordability, recovery benefits and residual exposure with service owners and finance.
Prepare the budget proposal and explain assumptions and unfunded requirements.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, investment priorities and a proposal template.
loop.output: Budget narrative linked to calculated figures and recorded decisions.
loop.check: Insert numbers deterministically; verify every stated benefit and unfunded requirement against approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported benefit claims remain blank for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables use templates, but the rationale must explain case-specific tradeoffs in plain language.

steps.what: Approve funding and accept the stated unfunded recovery requirements.
Record approved budget lines against cost centres and recovery initiatives.

tasks.design: An approved export from the {ERP} feeds a deterministic cost model with versioned assumptions and recovery options. A bounded loop extracts quotation conditions and drafts the rationale, while calculated figures populate the proposal in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} records funding approval before a validated budget import reaches the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance data, supplier conditions and recovery priorities were separate. The arithmetic was tractable, but assembling comparable assumptions took bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a reusable cost model, quotation extractor and import validator cheaper to build. Existing budget exports and approval features can handle much of the flow.
tasks.still_hard: Recovery benefits are uncertain and often cannot be reduced to a reliable financial return. Supplier pricing, internal capacity and competing funding demands still require human confirmation.
tasks.human_edge: The planner explains which recovery capability a spending choice buys and makes residual exposure understandable to decision makers.

ambition.what: Quarterly recovery-investment reprioritisation

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into reconciling tables and rewriting proposals. The planner can recommend reallocations between recovery options; spending authority remains with the budget holder.

reach.task: Compare investment options under uncertain operational benefits.
reach.learn: Sensitivity analysis, option appraisal and the limits of loss estimates.

reach.task: Plan shared spending on alternate workplaces and emergency supplies.
reach.learn: Capacity costing, renewal commitments and facilities budget cycles.

evidence.claim: Cost scenarios, sensitivity calculations and budget import validation can use deterministic rules.
Continuity investment priorities require judgement about affordability, recovery needs and residual exposure.

assumptions: The pilot covers one budget cycle, one finance export and a limited recovery-option catalogue.
Supplier quotations are already obtained; procurement negotiations are outside these estimates.
Contingency allowances and financial assumptions are explicit human inputs.
The final budget import is available through existing configuration; otherwise a deterministic connector is needed.
Consent and access include finance permissions and any applicable consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies if staffing estimates contain personal data; use aggregate role costs where sufficient.
unknowns: Can the planner obtain approved expenditure and commitment exports?
Which cost allocation, tax and accounting rules must the model follow?
Who can approve funding and accept unfunded recovery requirements?
Does the finance environment support validated budget imports?
research_questions: Which assumptions materially change the ranking of recovery investments?
Which quotation fields can move to structured submissions without shifting excessive work to service owners?
new_work: Review quotation exclusions and ambiguous cost units.
Maintain cost mappings, scenario formulas and import rules.
Refresh expired prices and capacity assumptions.
Investigate failed imports and differences from approved totals.
tasks.statement: Create business continuity and disaster recovery budgets.

tasks.short: Create and deliver continuity training, awareness materials, and follow-up learning.

steps.what: Agree audiences, learning goals, delivery format, and practical disruption scenarios.
Find current procedures, contact routes, and approved messages for the training.
Prepare slides, facilitator notes, quick guides, and practice questions.

loop.input: Approved procedures, audience brief, training templates, and permitted practice scenarios.
loop.output: Draft training pack with procedure references and answer keys.
loop.check: Verify references and required sections; flag unsupported instructions and check answers against approved procedures.
loop.stop: One generation and one revision per pack; unresolved instructions require manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble material; adapting explanations and practice questions to different roles requires language generation.

steps.what: Check operational accuracy, accessibility, and safety instructions before approving release.
Publish approved learning materials and enrol the agreed audiences.
Book sessions and send joining details to participants.
Deliver training, facilitate practice, and discuss participants' concerns and questions.
Record attendance, check completion, and assign agreed follow-up learning.

tasks.design: A template generator uses versioned procedures in {DOCS} and a bounded loop to draft role-specific materials. The safety lead approves instructions before configured flows publish to {LMS} and schedule sessions in {CALENDAR}. Human facilitation continues, while {LMS} handles completion records and agreed reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tailoring materials for different roles was labour intensive. Training administration and procedure updates were handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable layouts, source references, and bounded drafting reduce preparation time. Existing learning and calendar functions can handle administration.
tasks.still_hard: People need practice under realistic constraints. Language, accessibility, shift patterns, and local safety arrangements require deliberate adaptation.
tasks.human_edge: Build confidence, notice misunderstandings, and create enough trust for staff to disclose impractical procedures.

ambition.what: Continuity induction for temporary staff

tasks.altitude: The planner can spend more time facilitating practice and resolving questions. With delegated authority, they can choose audience-specific examples and delivery formats within approved safety instructions.

reach.task: Organize continuity induction for temporary staff and workplace support teams.
reach.learn: Audience access, shift coverage, accessible communication, and induction logistics.

evidence.claim: Template-based materials and bounded source-based drafting can reduce preparation work; human facilitation remains valuable.
Learning systems commonly support enrolment, completion records, and reminders.
GDPR applies to identifiable attendance records; consultation and employment requirements depend on national rules.

assumptions: The company combines live continuity sessions with materials held in {DOCS} and completion tracking in {LMS}.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are estimates for one training programme.
Follow-up rules concern learning administration and do not make employment decisions.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Whether temporary staff currently receive continuity induction.
Which languages, accessibility formats, and shift arrangements are needed.
Whether external staff can access {LMS}.
Who approves safety instructions and training audiences.
Whether completion records influence employment decisions.
research_questions: Can participants explain the correct first actions after using the generated materials?
Which questions reveal a faulty procedure rather than a training gap?
new_work: Review generated instructions, examples, and answer keys.
Refresh training when approved procedures change.
Handle enrolment exceptions and inaccessible learning formats.
Turn unresolved learner questions into procedure corrections.
tasks.statement: Create or administer training and awareness presentations or materials.

tasks.short: Keep continuity and disaster recovery knowledge current through reading, training, and professional exchange.

steps.what: Search professional resources and review notices for relevant learning opportunities.

loop.input: Notices and abstracts from an approved professional resource catalogue, plus learning priorities.
loop.output: A source-linked shortlist grouped by relevance, with reasons and dates.
loop.check: Verify source links and dates; planner reviews selections and periodically samples excluded items.
loop.stop: One classification per item and one batch repair; failed items remain visible without ranking.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keywords miss differently worded recovery methods and cannot reliably explain relevance to current learning needs.

steps.what: Choose reading, meetings, and training against current capability gaps.
Read technical literature and assess whether methods apply to recovery plans.
Attend professional meetings and training, practise methods, and question peers.
Record completion evidence and note potential changes to continuity practice.

tasks.design: A scheduled feed in the {WORKFLOW} gathers approved notices and uses a bounded classifier to prepare a source-linked learning shortlist in {DOCS}. The planner chooses and completes learning personally; configured records in the {LMS} capture completion evidence and a short, human-written proposal for applying the learning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Professional notices are scattered, and relevance depends on changing recovery priorities. Attendance records and practical lessons are often kept separately.
tasks.enabler_now: A small feed collector and bounded relevance classifier can reduce discovery work. Existing learning records can usually be configured without a separate application.
tasks.still_hard: Reading a summary does not build recovery judgement. Practical skill, peer trust, and assessing whether a method transfers to local conditions require participation.
tasks.human_edge: Ask useful questions, practise unfamiliar methods, and recognise when published advice fails under operational constraints.

ambition.what: Quarterly recovery-method clinic for site coordinators.

tasks.altitude: Discovery and record keeping take less time, leaving more room for practice and peer discussion. Formal decision rights do not change; applying a new recovery method still follows existing approval arrangements.

reach.task: Turn a promising recovery method into a small, measurable pilot.
reach.learn: Pilot scope, acceptance criteria, participant preparation, and explicit stop conditions.

evidence.claim: Feed collection, relevance shortlisting, and configured learning records can reduce learning administration.
Professional participation and practice remain human work; the digest contains no directly comparable learning case.

assumptions: The OTHER slot represents professional resource websites and catalogues.
The planner selects learning within an existing budget and remit.
Configured completion capture prefills records; the planner supplies the practical lesson.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates, with most learning time intentionally retained.
Only necessary learning records are retained under GDPR; any national consultation requirements need local assessment.
unknowns: Which professional resources can be accessed and reused under their terms?
Which qualifications require formal evidence of attendance or assessment?
Does the company have an LMS and an agreed learning budget?
Which recovery capability gaps should determine relevance?
research_questions: Does the shortlist surface useful material beyond familiar topics?
Which learning activities produce changes that survive an exercise?
new_work: Review shortlist relevance and sample excluded notices.
Maintain the approved resource catalogue and learning priorities.
Check completion evidence and write practical learning proposals.
Prepare and facilitate the recovery-method clinic if adopted.
tasks.statement: Attend professional meetings, read literature, and participate in training or other educational offerings to keep abreast of new developments and technologies related to disaster recovery and business continuity.

tasks.short: Test disaster recovery plans, assess results and track corrective actions.

steps.what: Gather approved plans, recovery objectives and previous findings from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}.
Write exercise scenarios, test steps, evidence requirements and pass criteria in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved plans, unresolved findings, objectives and an exercise template.
loop.output: Scenario narrative and proposed test steps linked to approved objectives.
loop.check: Validate objective coverage and evidence fields; planner checks realism and separates simulated from live actions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported test steps go to the recovery lead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates cover recurring checks, but scenario narratives require interpreting plan-specific dependencies.

steps.what: Approve exercise scope, live interventions, abort conditions and restoration responsibilities.
Arrange participants and test windows using {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Execute approved recovery tests using backup infrastructure in {OTHER} and capture results.
Debrief participants and judge whether recovery outcomes meet operational needs.
Compile timings, evidence references and agreed findings into an exercise report in {DOCS}.
Agree corrective actions, owners, deadlines and retests in {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: An exercise workflow in {WORKFLOW} assembles approved plans from {DOCS}, prepares scenario drafts and coordinates test windows through {CALENDAR}. Structured evidence capture feeds deterministic comparisons and report generation, while approved corrective actions enter {PROJECT} with owners and retest dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercise evidence arrived in inconsistent formats, and scheduling and report assembly crossed several teams. Live recovery tests required specialist control.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, scheduling rules and report templates already cover much of the paperwork. AI-assisted coding makes small evidence adapters more affordable, with bounded drafting for scenario text.
tasks.still_hard: Representative failure conditions, realistic workloads and safe test windows remain expensive. Passing a scripted test does not establish readiness for every disruption.
tasks.human_edge: The controller recognises misleading successes, pauses unsafe tests and draws candid lessons from participants.

ambition.what: Targeted retest decision after each critical corrective action closes

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time arranging exercises and compiling reports, and more time investigating weak recovery evidence. The controller retains live-test and abort authority; the planner can gain delegated authority to request scoped retests.

reach.task: Coordinate recovery test windows and corrective-action dependencies.
reach.learn: Change coordination, rollback planning and technical evidence acceptance.

evidence.claim: Recovery testing typically requires authorised scope, specialist execution, evidence review and corrective actions.
Scheduling, objective comparisons and structured report assembly can use deterministic automation; the digest supplies no direct recovery-testing case.

assumptions: The initial scope includes tabletop exercises and existing technical recovery procedures.
Build estimates cover coordination and evidence tooling, excluding new recovery infrastructure.
Time shares reflect a mixed exercise; technical tests and tabletop exercises will differ.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; consultation under national rules is assessed if participant recording or employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Existing backup infrastructure, test interfaces and approved runbooks.
Whether tests touch production services or third-party environments.
Available test windows, recovery specialists and evidence-retention requirements.
Whether employee participation or performance is recorded.
research_questions: Which recovery measures can be captured directly from existing test logs?
Which prior failures were missed by the existing pass criteria?
new_work: Review scenario drafts and maintain abort conditions.
Maintain evidence schemas and timestamp consistency.
Handle scheduling conflicts and missing evidence.
Validate corrective-action closure and decide when retesting is needed.
tasks.statement: Test documented disaster recovery strategies and plans.

tasks.short: Review continuity, crisis management, and disaster recovery plans for gaps and practical readiness.

steps.what: Retrieve current plans, exercise findings, and approved recovery requirements.
Check review dates, named owners, mandatory sections, and recorded recovery targets.
Read procedures for contradictions, missing dependencies, and unresolved exercise lessons.

loop.input: Current plan, approved recovery requirements, dependency map, and exercise findings.
loop.output: Candidate contradictions and omissions with source passages and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Verify document versions and quoted passages; planner checks each material finding against the requirement.
loop.stop: One review and one correction pass per plan; ambiguous or unsupported findings require manual assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedural meaning and contradictions span free-text sections with inconsistent wording.

steps.what: Challenge procedure feasibility and agree which gaps need correction or testing.
Write the review record with accepted findings and required corrective actions.
Assign agreed corrective actions and schedule the next review.

tasks.design: A configured review flow gathers controlled documents from the {DOCS}, runs deterministic completeness checks, and uses a bounded loop to flag source-linked procedural gaps. The plan owner decides the disposition of findings; templates produce the review record and approved actions flow into the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review evidence is scattered across plan versions, exercises, and recovery assessments. Simple checklists catch missing fields but miss contradictions in procedures.
tasks.enabler_now: Document metadata and structured review records support repeatable checks. Bounded comparison can surface candidate gaps for human challenge, with AI-assisted coding reducing the cost of the surrounding workflow.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible document does not establish recoverability. Practical readiness still needs owner challenge and exercises.
tasks.human_edge: The planner asks whether people could execute the procedure during disruption and recognises when evidence is too weak.

ambition.what: Change-triggered reviews of affected recovery procedures.

tasks.altitude: The planner uses more of the week for feasibility challenges and exercise design. A delegated review mandate could let them require a targeted test before recommending closure of a material finding.

reach.task: Verify corrective-action closure against evidence.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, finding severity, closure criteria, and independent verification.

evidence.claim: Continuity plan reviews commonly combine checklist checks, procedural assessment, owner challenge, and corrective-action tracking.
Deterministic checks suit structured requirements; free-text comparisons need source verification and human assessment.
The digest documents a generated report containing nonexistent sources, illustrating why generated findings need traceable evidence.

assumptions: Plans and assessments have identifiable approved versions.
Deterministic checks use structured fields or stable templates; ambiguous fields are marked unknown.
The system produces review findings rather than changing operational procedures automatically.
Build ranges include representative plan testing, access approval, and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which plan sections and approval requirements are mandatory.
Whether exercise findings and corrective actions have reliable status records.
Who can accept findings and require recovery tests.
Whether plans contain personal contact details requiring tighter access or retention.
research_questions: Which checks can existing document workflows perform?
How often does the bounded comparison miss material gaps or flag harmless wording differences?
Which plan changes should trigger a focused review?
new_work: Verify candidate gaps and dismiss unsupported findings.
Maintain checklists, source mappings, and comparison instructions.
Monitor document version selection and follow up on overdue corrective actions.
tasks.statement: Review existing disaster recovery, crisis management, or business continuity plans.

tasks.short: Define and implement monitoring and response methods for safety, operational, and compliance interruptions.

steps.what: Review interruption records, recurring failures, response delays, and unresolved actions.
Identify monitoring and response requirements in approved procedures and compliance guidance.

loop.input: Approved procedures and compliance guidance with versioned source identifiers.
loop.output: Candidate requirements, response owners, timing conditions, and source passages.
loop.check: Verify each source passage and retain qualifiers; planner checks completeness and interpretation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; ambiguous requirements go to the responsible specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements and exceptions appear in varied prose; keyword rules cannot reliably preserve their conditions.

steps.what: Agree detectable warning signs, response ownership, escalation paths, and operational constraints.
Specify indicators, thresholds, escalation timings, and checks for missing or stale signals.
Approve monitoring thresholds, escalation rules, and permitted automatic actions.
Configure monitoring feeds, notification rules, routing, and response timers.
Evaluate flagged interruptions, missed signals, false alarms, and response performance.
Agree and authorize corrective responses, assigning accountable operational owners.

tasks.design: A bounded extraction loop turns approved guidance in {DOCS} into candidate requirements for human review. Configured {WORKFLOW} rules connect permitted signals from {OPS_SYSTEM} and records from {HELPDESK}, checking thresholds and signal freshness. Views in {HELPDESK} show exceptions and response ownership; operational interventions require the incident coordinator's authorization.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were buried in prose, and signals had inconsistent ownership. Connecting monitoring, escalation, and response records required bespoke coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing routing and reporting functions cover much of the work. Faster integration development and bounded extraction make a limited monitoring service affordable.
tasks.still_hard: A silent signal can mean normal operation or failed monitoring. Alert fatigue, incomplete coverage, and safety consequences require realistic tests and operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret an interruption in context and coordinate a response when safety, service, and compliance priorities conflict.

ambition.what: Weekly review of interruption thresholds and missed warnings

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time collecting incident summaries and more time testing whether warnings lead to useful responses. Delegated authority can allow low-risk routing adjustments within approved limits; operational intervention rights remain with the incident coordinator.

reach.task: Evaluate whether interruption controls detect failures and produce effective corrective action.
reach.learn: Control effectiveness, missed-event analysis, false-alarm measurement, and corrective-action verification.

reach.task: Connect workplace service interruptions to continuity escalation.
reach.learn: Building-service signals, local response authority, and fallback communication.

evidence.claim: Threshold checks, signal-freshness checks, routing, and response timers can use deterministic rules.
Extracting requirements from varied prose benefits from bounded language processing and specialist review.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply according to the actual processing and AI use; national consultation rules vary.

assumptions: The typical implementation supports detection and coordination rather than controlling safety equipment.
Automatic actions are limited to approved internal notifications, ticket routing, and timers.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are estimates for one service or site.
The scoped monitoring uses service signals rather than individual employee surveillance.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Which warning signals exist, how fresh they are, and who maintains them.
Whether the available feeds remain accessible during disruption.
Which national rules and sector-specific obligations apply.
Whether monitoring includes identifiable employee activity.
Who can approve thresholds and authorize operational interventions.
research_questions: Do historical interruptions show warnings that the proposed rules would have detected?
Can missing or stale signals be distinguished from healthy service status?
Do test alerts reach an available owner through a functioning fallback channel?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve ambiguous obligations.
Investigate false alarms, missed interruptions, and stale feeds.
Maintain signal mappings, response rosters, and escalation rules.
Retest approved controls after service or procedure changes.
tasks.statement: Recommend or implement methods to monitor, evaluate, or enable resolution of safety, operations, or compliance interruptions.

tasks.short: Report continuity readiness, exercise results, recovery spending, and progress against agreed objectives.

steps.what: Export exercise actions, incident measures, recovery spending, and milestone status.
Read owner updates and supporting evidence for explanations and outstanding gaps.

loop.input: Approved owner updates, exercise debrief, and threat assessment.
loop.output: Source-linked facts, explanations, contradictions, and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each fact; planner checks contradictions and material explanations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unreadable or unsupported material goes to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Owners describe progress and causes in varied prose that fixed fields cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Reconcile figures, calculate measures, and assemble reporting tables.
Draft the report against objectives, explaining deviations and proposed actions.

loop.input: Validated reporting tables, evidence notes, unresolved exceptions, and report template.
loop.output: Draft continuity report with source references and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Insert numbers deterministically; verify references exist and unsupported explanations remain flagged.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per report; failed sections revert to the template for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables are deterministic, but concise explanations must combine varied evidence without inventing causes.

steps.what: Review material conclusions and approve the report for its intended audience.
Distribute the approved report and archive its supporting evidence.

tasks.design: Scheduled imports into the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile measures and feed reporting tables in {BI}; bounded extraction and drafting produce a source-linked report in {DOCS}. The planner resolves evidence exceptions, the continuity sponsor approves release, and the {WORKFLOW} distributes the approved version and records its evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measures, owner explanations, and evidence sit in different places. Reporting definitions and document assembly often lack reusable code.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes small connectors, validation rules, and report templates cheaper to build. Bounded text processing can organise narrative evidence, subject to source checks.
tasks.still_hard: Readiness measures can hide weak recovery assumptions. Explaining incomplete evidence and distinguishing completed actions from demonstrated capability still requires judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge reassuring claims, explain uncertainty, and connect findings to funding and operational decisions.

ambition.what: Monthly prioritisation of overdue recovery actions using evidence freshness and business exposure.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less of reporting week assembling tables and more time challenging weak evidence. A proposed delegated right is to request targeted evidence checks; funding and risk acceptance remain management decisions.

reach.task: Assess whether recovery spending produces measurable readiness improvements.
reach.learn: Cost attribution, consistent baselines, and the difference between correlation and demonstrated improvement.

evidence.claim: Scheduled imports, fixed calculations, templates, and approval routing can automate report assembly.
Narrative synthesis needs source validation and accountable review; the digest contains no continuity-reporting case.

assumptions: A mid-size company commonly combines exports, working spreadsheets, and document-based reporting.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Build ranges assume a small initial set of sources and existing identity and access controls.
Access estimates include consultation assessment where employee data is involved; required national procedures may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which reporting measures, definitions, recipients, and approval rights are agreed?
Which sources offer usable exports or interfaces?
How often do owners challenge figures or submit unsupported progress claims?
Does the evidence contain employee data requiring additional GDPR controls or consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which report sections are repeatedly rewritten despite unchanged evidence?
Can each material conclusion be traced to evidence in a representative past reporting cycle?
new_work: Resolve missing, conflicting, or stale evidence.
Review extracted explanations and material report conclusions.
Maintain metric definitions, source mappings, templates, and distribution permissions.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports summarizing operational results, financial performance, or accomplishments of specified objectives, goals, or plans.

tasks.short: Assess disruption impacts and agree recovery time targets and resource needs for critical functions.

steps.what: Collect process volumes, dependencies, contractual obligations, and prior disruption evidence.
Define disruption scenarios, impact thresholds, minimum service levels, and time-sensitive obligations.
Calculate impacts over outage periods and estimate minimum staffing, facilities, and system capacity.
Validate technical recovery capability and identify capacity or dependency constraints.
Reconcile competing recovery priorities and propose recovery targets and resource commitments.
Document impact assumptions, proposed recovery requirements, and unresolved gaps.
Approve recovery requirements and explicitly accept or escalate unresolved exposure.

tasks.design: Authorised exports from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} populate a structured impact assessment in the {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic calculations show outage impacts, resource needs, and sensitivity ranges; templates generate the assessment in the {DOCS} after owners reconcile feasibility and priorities, with approval attached to recovery requirements and risk acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Impact assumptions vary by department, supporting data takes effort to collect, and recovery capacity is difficult to compare across functions.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable assessment forms, available exports, and deterministic scenario calculations can standardise preparation. AI-assisted coding makes local calculation rules and report templates cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Impacts are uncertain and often nonlinear. Safety, customer harm, shared recovery capacity, and conflicting obligations require judgement and evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The planner exposes incompatible recovery promises and helps owners negotiate realistic priorities under limited resources.

ambition.what: Quarterly recovery-capacity trade-off reviews.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time challenging assumptions and resolving shared-resource conflicts. An explicit mandate could let them require feasibility evidence before submitting recovery targets; funding and residual-risk decisions remain with accountable owners.

reach.task: Assess alternative workplace capacity for priority services.
reach.learn: Site constraints, occupancy limits, utilities dependencies, and realistic mobilisation times.

reach.task: Estimate backlog and service recovery after an operational outage.
reach.learn: Throughput limits, backlog clearance, supplier dependencies, and constrained capacity allocation.

evidence.claim: Business impact assessments combine operational evidence, owner assumptions, outage impacts, recovery feasibility, and approved targets.
Structured assumptions support deterministic scenario calculations and report generation while recovery trade-offs remain human decisions.

assumptions: The initial scope covers selected critical functions and a manageable set of outage scenarios.
Contractual obligations are validated inputs rather than automatically interpreted legal conclusions.
Resource estimates use aggregate capacity rather than individual employee performance data.
Build ranges include calculation validation, a pilot assessment cycle, access, and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which impact thresholds and recovery requirements are already approved.
Availability and quality of operational volumes, resource rates, and recovery test evidence.
Which resources are shared across critical functions.
Who can commit recovery resources and accept residual exposure.
Applicable sector obligations, national rules, and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which impact relationships can be calculated reliably from available operational data?
How should uncertainty and nonfinancial harm be displayed alongside financial impacts?
Which recovery targets exceed tested capability when shared resources are considered?
new_work: Maintain calculation assumptions, resource rates, and scenario definitions.
Review stale inputs and unexplained changes in impact estimates.
Reconcile proposed targets with test evidence and shared recovery capacity.
Maintain integrations and document explicit risk acceptance.
tasks.statement: Analyze impact on, and risk to, essential business functions or information systems to identify acceptable recovery time periods and resource requirements.

tasks.short: Identify continuity improvements arising from business, regulatory, and industry changes.

steps.what: Collect change proposals, regulatory notices, and current continuity assessments.
Read proposals and map potential disruption to critical functions and dependencies.

loop.input: Change review pack, dependency map, and approved business impact assessment.
loop.output: Source-linked disruption hypotheses, affected functions, and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require source passages and valid function identifiers; planner checks material interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; unresolved interpretations enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative proposals describe operational changes in inconsistent language.

steps.what: Discuss disruption hypotheses and mitigation options with affected process owners.
Compare mitigation costs, disruption exposure, implementation effort, and residual risks.
Select mitigation priorities and accept or escalate residual exposure.
Record approved mitigations, owners, and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: An integration collects approved change material from the {PROJECT} and {DOCS}; a bounded reading loop prepares source-linked risk briefs. A deterministic comparison in the {WORKFLOW} shows costs, assumptions, and residual exposure, then records the risk owner's decision and creates actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change documents, dependency records, and mitigation estimates sit in separate places. Interpreting their operational consequences still requires experienced owners.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and configurable workflows support collection and follow-up. Bounded document extraction and AI-assisted coding make a tailored comparison tool cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Estimating rare disruption losses, interpreting regulatory changes, and securing funding remain uncertain and political.
tasks.human_edge: The planner challenges optimistic assumptions and finds mitigations that affected teams will actually adopt.

ambition.what: Monthly continuity triage of proposed business changes.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time testing mitigation choices with process owners. A delegated triage mandate could let them require a continuity review before project approval; funding and risk acceptance stay with accountable owners.

reach.task: Add continuity acceptance criteria to project stage reviews.
reach.learn: Project dependencies, decision deadlines, and how acceptance criteria are enforced.

evidence.claim: Change-risk assessment typically combines document review, owner discussions, option comparison, and accountable decisions.
Structured comparisons and action creation can use deterministic rules; narrative interpretation needs validation.
The digest documents fabricated citations in a generated report, supporting source verification for risk briefs.

assumptions: A shared continuity planner supports several departments in a mid-size European company.
An initial release covers selected change types and approved sources.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are checked for the actual use.
unknowns: Whether proposed changes are recorded before approval.
Which risk criteria and financial assumptions are approved.
Whether the planner can require a continuity review at project approval.
Available interfaces, access lead times, and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which change categories can be routed using existing metadata?
How accurately does bounded extraction identify affected functions in representative proposals?
Which uncertainty ranges make mitigation comparisons useful to risk owners?
new_work: Check source-linked risk briefs and resolve unsupported interpretations.
Maintain change-routing rules and approved comparison assumptions.
Handle missing records and monitor failed action creation.
tasks.statement: Identify opportunities for strategic improvement or mitigation of business interruption and other risks caused by business, regulatory, or industry-specific change initiatives.

tasks.short: Develop recovery plans for physical sites containing critical assets.

steps.what: Gather site inventories, drawings, supplier commitments and recovery objectives from {DOCS}, {ERP} and {CLM}.
Inspect critical assets, access routes, utilities and alternate workspace arrangements on site.
Choose relocation options, restoration sequence and specialist support with facilities and technology owners.
Draft site recovery procedures, dependencies and escalation instructions in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Verified site records, approved strategy and specialist-approved procedures.
loop.output: Source-linked site plan draft with missing facts explicitly flagged.
loop.check: Validate assets, owners and dependencies; planner checks every instruction against approved technical procedures.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; missing technical instructions go to specialists.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields can be merged directly, but site-specific constraints and approved procedures require narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Validate technical sequencing, access arrangements and safety dependencies with qualified specialists.
Approve recovery commitments, expenditure limits and residual site risks.
Publish controlled site packs in {DOCS} and arrange restricted offline copies.

tasks.design: A site register in {WORKFLOW} links asset records, drawings and supplier commitments from {ERP}, {DOCS} and {CLM}, with deterministic checks for missing owners and conflicting recovery dependencies. A bounded drafting loop assembles site plans from verified evidence; specialist and sponsor approvals release controlled online and offline packs through {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site drawings, asset records and supplier obligations were maintained separately. Bespoke plan assembly was expensive, while physical verification could not be inferred from records.
tasks.enabler_now: Lightweight registers and document generators can be built more cheaply with AI-assisted coding. A bounded loop can organise approved narrative procedures without inventing technical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Actual utility resilience, alternate-site capacity and supplier availability require verification. Specialist engineering review and physical improvements remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Site specialists recognise physical constraints and unsafe assumptions that inventories and drawings miss.

ambition.what: Pre-move recovery-readiness assessment for proposed site changes

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time inspecting weak dependencies with facilities and technology owners. They can gain a formal readiness-review role before site changes, while engineering acceptance and expenditure remain with accountable specialists and management.

reach.task: Assess utility dependencies and alternate workspace readiness.
reach.learn: Site inspection methods, asset criticality and limits of engineering competence.

evidence.claim: Site recovery planning requires physical verification and coordination between facilities, technology and operational owners.
Registers, dependency checks and controlled document assembly are feasible deterministic components; no direct site-recovery case appears in the digest.
The digest documents invented sources in a generated report, supporting source checks before technical plan approval.

assumptions: The first release covers one critical site with existing drawings and designated specialists.
Build estimates exclude engineering surveys, alternate-site procurement and physical remediation.
Site plans use specialist-approved technical procedures.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation follows national rules where workplace or personal-data arrangements change.
unknowns: Number of sites, asset classes and quality of existing drawings.
Whether alternate locations and supplier recovery commitments have been tested.
Access restrictions on security-sensitive site information.
Required specialist approvals and applicable employee consultation.
research_questions: Which physical dependencies are missing from current asset records?
Which site changes should automatically trigger a readiness review?
new_work: Verify imported site records and resolve stale drawings.
Review drafted instructions with qualified specialists.
Maintain dependency checks and change-trigger rules.
Refresh restricted offline packs and supplier commitments.
tasks.statement: Develop disaster recovery plans for physical locations with critical assets, such as data centers.

tasks.short: Develop realistic disruption scenarios and workable sequences for restoring operations.

steps.what: Review impact assessments, incidents, dependencies and existing recovery plans.
Map outage duration, capacity constraints and dependencies against recovery requirements.
Choose credible disruption conditions and recovery options with service owners.
Write scenario timelines, recovery sequences and exercise prompts.

loop.input: Chosen parameters, validated constraints, recovery options and exercise templates.
loop.output: Scenario narratives, event prompts and proposed recovery sequences.
loop.check: Check timings and dependencies deterministically; distinguish exercise fiction from factual capabilities and flag unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: Generate at most three variants and one correction pass; infeasible or unsupported variants return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates generate structure, but coherent narratives and prompts must combine varied disruption conditions.

steps.what: Challenge feasibility and approve scenarios for the intended exercise.
Publish the approved scenario pack with controlled access and version details.
Record unresolved capability gaps and assign follow-up work.

tasks.design: A deterministic constraint model on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines approved dependencies, recovery targets and capacity assumptions from the {DOCS} and structured exports. A bounded loop turns chosen conditions into scenario packs, with calculated timings inserted by code. Service owners approve suitability before the {WORKFLOW} publishes the pack and creates follow-up actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source plans were fragmented and scenario writing was bespoke. Organisations also lacked reliable capacity and dependency data for automatic feasibility checks.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes small constraint models and reusable pack generators practical. Bounded drafting can vary narratives while keeping factual capability claims tied to approved inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Unknown dependencies and correlated failures limit the model. A plausible narrative does not prove that recovery will succeed, and restoration durations need operational evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The planner chooses disruptions that expose meaningful weaknesses and challenges reassuring assumptions without making the exercise pointless.

ambition.what: Compound-disruption exercise packs for small service teams

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling packs and more time testing assumptions with operators. They can propose a broader exercise programme; service owners retain authority over feasibility claims and exercise participation.

reach.task: Model recovery options when sites, carriers or suppliers become unavailable.
reach.learn: Capacity bottlenecks, lead-time distributions and dependency propagation.

reach.task: Map restoration prerequisites between applications and infrastructure.
reach.learn: Service dependencies, data consistency and evidence from restoration tests.

evidence.claim: Dependency, timing and capacity constraints can be checked with deterministic models when inputs are explicit.
Generated scenario narratives require operational review and do not validate recovery capabilities.

assumptions: The pilot uses a bounded set of critical services and tabletop scenarios.
Recovery targets and capacity estimates remain supplied or validated by service owners.
The automation prior is reduced because scenario credibility and feasibility remain substantial human work.
Build estimates exclude live failover tooling and full operational simulation.
Consent and access cover sensitive plan permissions and any exercise-related consultation required by national rules.
GDPR applies to personal data in incident records; EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use.
unknowns: How current and complete are dependency and capacity records?
Which restoration durations have been tested rather than estimated?
Who may approve scenarios involving multiple services?
Which scenario details must remain restricted before an exercise?
research_questions: Which compound failures reveal gaps that single-service exercises miss?
How well do calculated recovery sequences match observed exercise results?
Which scenario elements need narrative generation rather than parameterised templates?
new_work: Review generated narratives for unsupported capability claims.
Maintain constraint rules, scenario templates and capacity assumptions.
Compare model assumptions with exercise observations.
Manage scenario access and retire obsolete packs.
tasks.statement: Create scenarios to reestablish operations from various types of business disruptions.

tasks.short: Integrate continuity plans across teams and coordinate their operation during disruptions.

steps.what: Retrieve current plans, recovery requirements and dependency records.
Request changes and readiness confirmations from service owners.
Compare recovery sequences, dependencies and resource commitments across plans.

loop.input: Versioned plans, readiness updates and a structured dependency register.
loop.output: Proposed conflicts with source passages and affected services.
loop.check: Validate service identifiers, references and timing constraints; the planner checks substantive conflicts.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass per plan batch; unresolved conflicts enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Timing checks are deterministic, but dependencies and commitments also appear in inconsistent prose.

steps.what: Agree recovery priorities and resolve competing resource commitments.
Revise shared procedures, escalation paths and recovery checklists.

loop.input: Approved integration decisions, current procedures and controlled templates.
loop.output: Tracked plan revisions and a change summary.
loop.check: Check required sections and references; reject unsupported instructions and altered recovery targets.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per plan; unresolved passages return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble the pack, but procedural wording must reflect decisions expressed in free text.

steps.what: Approve the integrated plans and accept outstanding readiness limitations.
Publish approved plans and assign readiness actions.
Coordinate activation and escalate recovery conflicts during a disruption.

tasks.design: A portable register in the {WORKFLOW} links versioned plans in the {DOCS} to dependencies, owners and readiness actions in the {PROJECT}. Deterministic checks flag timing conflicts; bounded model loops propose prose conflicts and tracked revisions with source references. Approval releases each plan, while activation and recovery tradeoffs remain with the incident commander.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans used inconsistent wording and separate ownership. Keeping dependencies and versions aligned required repeated coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building importers, comparison checks and revision generators. Structured owner confirmations reduce reconciliation work without requiring a new reasoning breakthrough.
