tasks.still_hard: Shared recovery resources, uncertain incident information and unavailable services require negotiation. The coordination tools also need an accessible fallback during outages.
tasks.human_edge: The planner secures credible commitments and recognises when a technically consistent plan cannot work under pressure.

ambition.what: Monthly cross-service recovery-order reviews

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing versions to resolving dependency conflicts and rehearsing recovery choices. The planner can propose cross-service priorities more often; risk acceptance and activation rights remain with designated leaders.

reach.task: Sequence recovery dependencies across technology changes.
reach.learn: Change windows, restoration prerequisites and evidence of successful recovery.

reach.task: Confirm alternate-site readiness and capacity.
reach.learn: Site access, utilities, occupancy constraints and fallback communications.

evidence.claim: Version control, structured confirmations and dependency checks can support continuity-plan integration deterministically.
Live recovery coordination needs human judgement when information and resource availability change.

assumptions: The pilot covers a small set of critical services and approved file exports.
Time shares describe ordinary integration work; disruption periods can make live coordination dominant.
Service owners still confirm readiness; reminders do not establish readiness.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a pilot, not a replacement for every recovery system.
Consent and access include permissions and any employee consultation required by national rules; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
GDPR applies to personal contact data; EU AI Act obligations depend on the intended use.

Who may approve plans, accept readiness exceptions and authorise activation?
Which exports, interfaces and offline communication channels are available?
Do national rules or existing agreements require employee consultation for the proposed changes?

Can the coordination pack remain usable when primary identity, communication or document services fail?

Maintain service identifiers, dependency rules and approval routes.
Resolve missing owner confirmations and stale source records.
Test offline access and fallback communications.
tasks.statement: Conduct or oversee contingency plan integration and operation.

tasks.short: Develop emergency plans covering recovery priorities, communications, critical processes and temporary shutdowns.

steps.what: Collect process inventories, contacts and existing plans from {DOCS}, {HCM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Discuss disruption impacts, dependencies and minimum service needs with process owners.
Agree recovery priorities, shutdown triggers, decision rights and acceptable service compromises.
Write recovery procedures, communications templates and departmental shutdown instructions in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved recovery objectives, recovery strategy, verified baseline and plan template.
loop.output: Source-linked continuity plan draft with unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and references; planner checks feasibility, dependencies and every operational instruction.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; unresolved facts return to process owners.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble fixed fields, but process-specific instructions require interpreting approved narrative evidence.

steps.what: Review the plan and approve organisational commitments and delegated emergency powers.
Publish the approved version in {DOCS} and distribute controlled copies through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A governed baseline in {DATA_PLATFORM} joins approved records from {DOCS}, {HCM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; deterministic checks expose missing owners and inconsistent dependencies. A bounded drafting loop fills plan sections from approved evidence, while {WORKFLOW} routes decisions and publishes approved versions through {DOCS}, including controlled offline packs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were fragmented, ownership was unclear and bespoke document assembly was costly. Recovery compromises still required agreement across departments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing versioning and approval features cover publication. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation rules and document generators; bounded drafting handles narrative sections.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden dependencies, disputed recovery priorities and resource commitments remain difficult. A readable plan can still be operationally impossible.
tasks.human_edge: The planner exposes competing needs, challenges optimistic assumptions and secures commitments that hold during disruption.

ambition.what: Quarterly recovery-priority review after material process changes

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling documents and more time challenging recovery assumptions with process owners. Executives retain emergency powers and spending decisions; the planner can gain delegated authority to convene change-triggered reviews.

reach.task: Map cross-department dependencies and minimum viable services.
reach.learn: Process mapping, dependency analysis and evidence-based impact estimation.

evidence.claim: Continuity planning commonly combines records gathering, owner workshops, drafting and management approval; this decomposition is a model-based estimate.
Deterministic validation and source-grounded drafting are plausible components; the digest supplies no direct continuity-planning implementation case.
The digest documents a report containing invented sources, supporting explicit source validation for generated plans.

assumptions: Scope is one mid-size company with existing process owners and a designated executive sponsor.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Estimates cover a first usable implementation using existing hosting and identity controls.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed data use.
unknowns: Completeness and ownership of process inventories and recovery objectives.
Available export interfaces and publication features in existing systems.
Delegated emergency powers and the approval route for shutdown decisions.
Employee data fields needed and applicable consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which plan defects are found most often during exercises?
Can dependency and document validation provide most of the benefit before adding drafting?
new_work: Review generated instructions against approved evidence.
Resolve missing owners and conflicting dependency records.
Maintain templates, connectors, access controls and distribution rules.
Check offline packs after each approved release.
tasks.statement: Develop emergency management plans for recovery decision making and communications, continuity of critical departmental processes, or temporary shut-down of non-critical departments to ensure continuity of operation and governance.

tasks.short: Coordinate lawful intelligence collection on fraud, cyber threats, hostile acts, and infrastructure failure.

steps.what: Agree collection questions, permitted sources, responsibilities, and handling restrictions.
Collect authorised security monitoring, finance, infrastructure, and public advisory records.
Read specialist submissions and extract relevant events, sources, dates, and limitations.

loop.input: Authorised specialist submissions and the approved collection brief.
loop.output: Source-linked event records with dates, affected dependencies, uncertainty, and handling labels.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source passages; planner checks material omissions and preserves allegations as unverified.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per submission; failures remain visible for manual processing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Submissions describe events and limitations in inconsistent prose rather than stable fields.

steps.what: Check provenance, freshness, completeness, and duplicate records against the collection brief.
Resolve collection gaps and source limitations with responsible specialists.
File the validated intelligence and notify authorised assessors of availability and gaps.

tasks.design: Read-only connectors on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collect approved records from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, {HELPDESK}, and authorised sources in {OTHER}, retaining provenance and collection logs. A bounded extractor prepares specialist submissions, deterministic checks flag gaps, and the {WORKFLOW} releases the validated set in {DOCS} only to authorised assessors.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources have separate owners, access restrictions, formats, and release schedules. Technical collection is easier than agreeing what may lawfully be collected and shared.
tasks.enabler_now: Small read-only connectors, structured evidence records, and quality checks are cheaper to build. Bounded extraction can reduce rekeying while retaining the original source.
tasks.still_hard: Source credibility, lawful purpose, confidential investigations, and information-sharing limits remain difficult. Collection cannot guarantee prevention of an attack or failure.
tasks.human_edge: Earn specialist cooperation, judge collection proportionality, and recognise when missing intelligence needs direct investigation.

ambition.what: A dependency-specific intelligence brief for regional site coordinators.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time chasing routine extracts and more time resolving coverage gaps. A proposed delegated right is to request missing evidence within the approved collection brief; new sources and purposes require owner authorisation.

reach.task: Identify disruption signals affecting critical supply and transport dependencies.
reach.learn: Supplier concentration, route dependencies, lead-time variability, and limitations of partner intelligence.

reach.task: Maintain reliable site contacts and infrastructure evidence for continuity assessment.
reach.learn: Local infrastructure ownership, evidence freshness, and escalation responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Read-only imports, provenance records, freshness checks, and access-controlled releases are deterministic building blocks.
Narrative extraction can support collection administration but does not establish source truth.
The digest provides no directly comparable continuity intelligence-collection case or measured saving.

assumptions: Specialists retain responsibility for security investigations and source-system operations.
The OTHER slot represents security monitoring systems and public advisory feeds.
Collection uses authorised sources and does not introduce covert monitoring or automated adverse decisions.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are estimates for a limited initial source set.
GDPR requires purpose, access, retention, and personal-data controls; assess DPIA needs and applicable EU AI Act obligations.
Consultation and access ranges include preparation and review; national procedures or source-owner decisions may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: What collection purposes, legal bases, retention periods, and sharing restrictions apply?
Which specialists own fraud, cyber, physical security, and infrastructure intelligence?
Which sources permit automated access and onward sharing?
Would the proposed processing require a DPIA or employee consultation under national rules?
Which site coordinators may receive which intelligence categories?
research_questions: Which collection gaps most often prevent a useful threat assessment?
Can source-level permissions and handling labels survive every export and downstream release?
Which existing exports or configured feeds remove the need for custom connectors?
new_work: Review extraction omissions, provenance failures, and unresolved collection gaps.
Maintain connectors, source owners, collection scope, and handling labels.
Review access, retention, and source-use permissions.
Prepare restricted site briefs if the new audience is approved.
tasks.statement: Conduct or oversee collection of corporate intelligence to avoid fraud, financial crime, cyber attack, terrorism, and infrastructure failure.

tasks.short: Assess intelligence for threats to people, assets, information, and infrastructure.

steps.what: Retrieve collected intelligence, incident records, and affected asset details.
Compare incident patterns, exposure measures, and changes against previous periods.
Read narrative intelligence and identify possible threats, dependencies, and contradictory signals.

loop.input: Approved narrative intelligence, trend tables, asset dependencies, and threshold exceptions.
loop.output: Provisional threat hypotheses with supporting passages, contradictions, and uncertainty.
loop.check: Require source references and separate observations from inference; specialists test hypotheses in the next step.
loop.stop: One analysis and one repair per evidence batch; missing evidence and failed outputs enter specialist review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Novel warnings depend on meaning and context across narratives; fixed thresholds cover only known patterns.

steps.what: Test hypotheses with security, facilities, finance, and operations specialists.
Rank threats and agree escalation with the risk owner.
Send the agreed advisory and record follow-up owners.

tasks.design: The {DATA_PLATFORM} joins approved intelligence to incident and asset records, while deterministic measures feed {BI}. A bounded loop drafts source-linked hypotheses for specialist discussion; the risk owner approves advisories routed through the {WORKFLOW}, while existing urgent alert routes continue independently.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence uses inconsistent identifiers and mixes numerical trends with narrative warnings. Threat interpretation cannot be reduced to a stable checklist.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and transparent calculations are cheaper to implement. Bounded models can organise narrative signals for specialist examination without deciding the operational response.
tasks.still_hard: Rare threats provide little validation data. Missing signals, unreliable sources, and false reassurance can have serious consequences.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise operational context, challenge plausible stories, and decide when uncertainty itself warrants escalation.

ambition.what: Weekly reassessment of exposure for the highest-priority recovery dependencies.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time testing threat hypotheses with specialists and less time compiling evidence. A proposed delegated right is to call focused validation reviews; protective actions and risk acceptance remain with authorised owners.

reach.task: Assess which site dependencies need temporary protection during a developing disruption.
reach.learn: Utility dependencies, site operating limits, and the evidence needed for safe occupancy decisions.

reach.task: Map technical failures to business recovery dependencies.
reach.learn: Service dependency mapping, recovery evidence, and technical incident severity.

evidence.claim: Deterministic trend calculations and asset joins can support repeatable threat assessment.
Model-generated threat hypotheses require specialist validation and cannot establish the absence of threats.
The digest provides no directly comparable continuity threat-analysis implementation or measured benefit.

assumptions: The planner assesses business exposure with specialists rather than replacing security operations.
The OTHER slot represents an asset inventory in the retrieval step.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are estimates; judgement remains the largest constraint.
GDPR applies to personal data, and EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use.
Access estimates include assessment of national consultation requirements; formal procedures may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which threats and dependencies fall within the planner's remit?
How complete and current is the asset register?
Who can authorise advisories, operational restrictions, and emergency escalation?
Do inputs include employee monitoring, individual allegations, or other sensitive personal data?
Which existing urgent alert routes must operate independently?
research_questions: Can a historical review recover known warning signals without excessive irrelevant hypotheses?
Which evidence gaps would make the assessment unsafe to use?
Which threat categories are adequately handled by existing configured thresholds?
new_work: Test hypotheses and investigate contradictory evidence.
Review missed signals and false alarms after exercises or incidents.
Maintain dependency mappings, thresholds, source permissions, and evaluation examples.
Check that model failures cannot delay established emergency escalation.
tasks.statement: Analyze corporate intelligence data to identify trends, patterns, or warnings indicating threats to security of people, assets, information, or infrastructure.

role_batches.altitude: The continuity planner moves from document assembly and coordination toward validating recovery evidence, exposing dependencies and securing practical commitments. Any added authority concerns convening reviews and approved drills; emergency activation, engineering acceptance and risk acceptance remain explicitly delegated management decisions.

Information technology project managers: coordinate recovery testing and corrective-action dependencies.
Management analysts: map minimum viable services and cross-department impacts.
Administrative services managers: resolve communication coverage and deputy arrangements.
skills_to_grow: Structured dependency modelling and data validation.
Exercise design and evidence-based recovery assessment.
Source-grounded review of generated procedures.
Workflow configuration, access control and integration ownership.
Cross-functional negotiation and incident decision facilitation.
GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and consultation under national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring recovery-readiness service that reviews planned operational changes, commissions targeted retests and presents unresolved recovery gaps for explicit management decisions.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from collecting evidence and maintaining documents toward challenging recovery claims, designing tests, and resolving cross-functional trade-offs. Decision rights expand only through an explicit mandate to require evidence or targeted reviews; risk acceptance and spending remain with accountable owners.
reach: Project management specialists: put continuity criteria into project approval and delivery.
Computer systems analysts: validate dependencies that determine recovery order.
Quality control systems managers: close corrective actions against sufficient evidence.
Facilities managers and logistics analysts: test recovery assumptions against physical capacity.
skills_to_grow: Structured dependency modelling and data-quality checks.
Scenario calculations, uncertainty ranges, and capacity constraints.
Source verification and evaluation of bounded document comparisons.
Exercise design and evidence-based corrective-action closure.
Facilitation of competing recovery priorities.
GDPR, EU AI Act applicability, and relevant national consultation rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring recovery-readiness review that connects proposed changes, dependency changes, impact assumptions, and exercise evidence to specific decisions about testing, mitigation, and capacity.

role_batches.altitude: The continuity planner's week shifts toward recovery trade-offs, realistic exercises, facilitation, and control effectiveness. Delegated rights can cover small tool configurations, training formats, and low-risk routing changes within approved limits; risk acceptance and operational intervention stay with their accountable owners.
reach: Project management specialists: translate recovery gaps into verifiable remediation work.
Computer systems analysts: configure and test continuity tools against dependency failures.
Facilities managers: connect physical workplace constraints with recovery and escalation arrangements.
Quality control systems managers: test whether continuity controls detect failures and drive effective correction.

Source checking and review of bounded model outputs.
Failure testing, fallback access, and rollback planning.

GDPR handling, AI-use assessment, and consultation under applicable national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a small-team continuity service combining practical tool clinics, temporary-staff induction, and recurring failure reviews. Give teams tested recovery tools and clear escalation routes, with measured evidence of where recovery still depends on fragile assumptions.

role_batches.altitude: The continuity planner spends more time challenging recovery assumptions, negotiating shared capacity and testing readiness. Better preparation supports more frequent recommendations; funding, legal interpretation, risk acceptance and incident command remain explicit decision rights.
reach: Information technology project management: sequence restoration dependencies and validate recovery evidence.
Facilities management: assess alternate-site capacity and fallback communications.
Management analysis: compare recovery investments under uncertain benefits.
Quality control systems management: connect obligations, procedures and evidence.

Recovery cost modelling and sensitivity analysis
Exercise design and facilitation

role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a rolling recovery-options service that connects investment choices, dependency conflicts and exercise evidence. Use it to bring specific readiness decisions to authorised leaders throughout the year.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from assembling evidence to testing whether recovery assumptions hold. Proposed delegated rights cover targeted evidence requests and focused validation reviews; risk acceptance, emergency command, and spending remain with authorised owners.
reach: Work with facilities managers on site dependencies and practical recovery limits.
Work with computer systems analysts on service dependencies and recovery evidence.
Work with logistics analysts on supplier and transport disruption exposure.
Work with management analysts on readiness measures and recovery investment.

Interpret data quality, provenance, and uncertainty.
Validate model outputs against source material.
Facilitate specialist challenge and escalation decisions.
Understand personal-data handling and applicable national consultation requirements.
Scope small integrations and maintain transparent reporting rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run an evidence-led continuity service that reassesses critical dependencies regularly, gives site coordinators useful intelligence, and tests new recovery methods through small exercises.

role_batches.altitude: The continuity planner becomes a better-prepared coordinator of focused enquiries. Business owners retain operational judgement, and risk owners retain collection approval.
reach: Logistics dependency analysis with logistics analysts.
Application dependency mapping with computer systems analysts.
